panels.denominator: NASA agency information-security program under the stated fiscal-year IG metrics
panels.method: Annual independent FISMA evaluation using the applicable IG metrics
panels.attribution: NASA Office of Inspector General and its independent evaluator
reporting_breaks: The FY 2023 evaluation period ended May 31, 2023; annual metric sets can change.
missing_data: Track FY 2025 metrics, function-level maturity, control testing, authorization age, remediation, incidents, recovery, affected services, and mission effects.

panels.comparison_boundary: Publish the repeated agency-program rating only. Do not infer unchanged cyber risk, system performance, incidents, mission effect, or equivalence with another agency.

temporal_order.statement: NASA remained at FISMA Level 3 across FY 2022-FY 2024.
NASA assigned zero-trust leadership, planned phased corporate implementation, and funded corporate initiatives while mission and JPL owners retained separate responsibilities.
Non-corporate implementation had not begun; legacy systems, distributed ownership, and unknown non-corporate costs remained open.
The later FY 2025 FISMA evaluation again reported Level 3, Consistently Implemented.

panels.driver_constraint_attribution: NASA OIG independently reports both the implementation condition and the annual maturity result.
panels.independent_validation: Independent oversight supplies two different official records; neither report validates a causal link between them.
panels.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Track FY 2026 FISMA results, pillar-level implementation across corporate and non-corporate systems, tested-control operation, incidents, recovery, service effects, and mission outcomes.

panels.denominator: DHS department information-security program under the stated fiscal-year IG metrics
panels.method: Annual independent FISMA evaluation with function-level maturity testing

temporal_order.statement: DHS moved from ineffective in FY 2021 to effective in FY 2022 and FY 2023.
DHS and CISA continued operating the government-wide CDM program for asset visibility and network monitoring.
GAO identified incomplete guidance, data-quality controls, endpoint onboarding, and cloud-asset management.
DHS OIG rated the FY 2024 department program effective, with function ratings of Level 4 or Level 5.

panels.driver_constraint_attribution: DHS OIG reports the department result; GAO independently reports CDM implementation constraints.
panels.independent_validation: Two independent oversight bodies support the coexistence of the records, not a causal relationship.
panels.causal_boundary: Temporal order and association may be described; the record does not establish causation.
next_records: Track FY 2025 department and component ratings, recommendation closure evidence, CDM data quality, endpoint coverage, cloud assets, incidents, recovery, and service effects.

The FY 2025 evaluation again rated the HHS information-security program Not Effective.
